Morocco have been banned from the next two African Nations Cups and fined $1m (£656,000) for pulling out of hosting this year’s competition, the Confederation of African Football has announced.
Caf also ordered the Moroccan Football Federation to pay compensation of €8m (£5.9m) for losses sustained by CAF, its stakeholders and partners as a result of its decision not to host the tournament.

Eventual champions Ivory Coast emerged as the new kings of the continent and were rewarded with a $1.5 million prize money. The money goes to the Ivorian Football Association which will then, if prior agreements exist, pay out bonuses to members of the 2015 African Cup of Nations winning squad. The total prize money pot for AFCON 2015 participants amounted to $10 million.

While the 2015 edition of the African Cup of Nations went on in Equatorial Guinea, erstwhile hosts Morocco were sanctioned for ‘refusing’ to abide by the hosting agreement signed with CAF and as a result, the football body announced that Morocco had been banned from the next two AFCON tournaments (2017 and 2019). CAF also slapped Morocco with a fine of $1 million for its withdrawal and in addition demanded a total compensation package of around $9 million ‘for all material damage sustained by CAF, stakeholders and partners’.
